correctness.rationale: For \(S=\sqrt{ab}\), every original solution gives a rational \(z=ay/S\) whose square is the integer \(x^{2n}-c^{2n}\), forcing \(z\in\mathbb Z\). The equation then factors exactly as \((x^n-z)(x^n+z)=c^{2n}\), yielding the stated necessary and sufficient signed-divisor conditions. Conversely the conditions reconstruct integral \(y\). In the source's \(t=1\) branch, equation (18) is \(w^2-v^2=N>0\), so factorization gives finitely many solutions; the explicit \(N=3\) witness has exactly four. The standalone verifier matches the parametrization against exhaustive direct search for \(1\le N\le500\) and checks 96 full-equation cases.
